passage: At two in the morning in their Mexico City flat, Jana sat up and pointed at the door, whimpering. A tall dark shape stood there. Mamá Camila came in, switched on the small night light and sat on the bed. "It's your coat on the hook, cariño. See? Just the coat." She spoke slowly and held Jana close until the shape turned into a coat. She never mentioned monsters. Jana pressed her cheek to Camila's shoulder and her whimper faded.

qa.q: What was the dark shape on the door?
qa.a: It was the coat on the hook.

qa.q: What was Jana feeling when she pointed at the door, and how can you tell?
qa.a: She was frightened, since she whimpered and sat up, because a shadow can look very real to a child who cannot yet tell real from imagined.

qa.q: What else could Camila do on other nights to help Jana feel safe?
qa.a: Keep the night light on, hang the coat somewhere else, and keep using a calm voice and closeness, without joking about monsters.

qa.q: How might Camila have felt being woken at two in the morning?
qa.a: She may have been tired, yet her slow voice and closeness show she put comforting Jana first.

grounding: Shows a toddler frightened by a shadow at bedtime and a parent responding with a night light, calm voice and closeness.

passage: Her father, Rafiq, closed the door of the back room of the farmhouse, next to where the goats were tied, and turned the latch. "Sleep. No crying." Two-year-old Jahnavi called, "Papa, Papa," again and again. Nobody came. After a long while the room went quiet. Dadi, hearing the silence, lifted the latch and found her curled up, eyes open, thumb in her mouth, not reaching up. Dadi lay down beside her and hummed. Later Dadi asked Rafiq to sit near Jahnavi at bedtime instead.

qa.q: What did Rafiq say as he closed the door?
qa.a: He said, "Sleep. No crying."

qa.q: Why did the room go quiet, and what cue shows it was not calm?
qa.a: Jahnavi may have stopped because nobody answered, not because she was soothed. Dadi found her awake, curled up and not reaching up.

qa.q: What could Rafiq do at bedtime to build better sleep habits?
qa.a: Stay near and respond warmly with a short, steady routine, and let Jahnavi settle with him close by.

qa.q: What might Dadi have felt on finding Jahnavi like that?
qa.a: Dadi probably felt worried and tender toward Jahnavi, which is why she lay down beside her and hummed.

grounding: Shows a very young child shut in alone and ignored while crying until she gives up, and a grandmother responding with warmth.

passage:
"Mummy, done!" Jasleen shouted from the potty.
Alka peeked in. "You did a wee in the potty! Yay, Jasleen!" She clapped once.
Jasleen beamed and clapped back. "Wash hands?"
"Wash hands!"
Later there was a small puddle by the sofa.
"Oops, that's okay," said Alka. "Let's get a cloth. Next time."
Jasleen giggled and rubbed the floor with the cloth.

qa.q: What did Jasleen shout from the potty?
qa.a: Jasleen shouted, "Mummy, done!"

qa.q: How does Jasleen feel after Alka's cheer, and how can you tell?
qa.a: Jasleen feels proud, since she beams, claps back and is happy to go and wash hands.

qa.q: Why is simple praise and a calm reaction to the puddle a good approach?
qa.a: It keeps it light so there is no pressure, and accidents are treated as normal because bodies learn on their own timetable. 🙂

qa.q: How might Alka be feeling about the potty and the puddle?
qa.a: She is probably pleased about the success and calm about the puddle, showing she is not in a rush.

grounding: Shows a toddler beaming after a potty success with warm simple praise, and a puddle met kindly with a cloth.

passage: Nursery note, Monday. Devika, two, had an accident during story time. She stood stock-still and hid her hands behind her back. Her father Wasim had mentioned that at home he laughed and called her "smelly". Today she tried to stuff the wet clothes into her bag rather than tell me. I took her to change and said, "That happens. It's okay. We'll try again later." Her shoulders came down. I have asked to speak to Wasim privately about staying calm.

qa.q: When did Devika's accident happen?
qa.a: It happened during story time.

qa.q: What was Devika feeling after the accident, and what shows it?
qa.a: She seemed ashamed and afraid of being caught, since she stood still, hid her hands and tried to stuff the wet clothes into her bag.

qa.q: What could Wasim do at home the next time there is an accident?
qa.a: Clean up calmly, say it is okay, and try again another day without laughing or name-calling.

qa.q: How might Wasim have felt when he laughed at the accident?
qa.a: He may have felt awkward or unsure how to react, and laughing was a nervous way to cope without meaning to hurt Devika.

grounding: Shows a toddler ashamed after being laughed at for toileting accidents, hiding them, and a teacher calmly reassuring her.

passage:
Monday. "Potty time!" said her father, Yash. Aadhya, two, shook her head, clamped her legs together and said, "No!" Yash sighed and let it go.
Wednesday. "Which potty seat, the frog or the star?" She still said no. Yash shrugged. "Okay, later."
Sunday. Yash set the frog potty in the living room and said nothing. Aadhya walked over, sat on it fully clothed with her doll, and stayed there, humming.

qa.q: Which two potty choices did Yash offer on Wednesday?
qa.a: He offered the frog potty seat or the star.

qa.q: Why might Aadhya clamp her legs and say "No!", and what does she seem to want to feel?
qa.a: She may be claiming control over her own body, and pressure would only make her hold on harder.

qa.q: What did Yash do that lowered the pressure?
qa.a: He offered choices, took the refusals calmly, and put the potty in the living room without comment, giving her time.

qa.q: How might Yash have felt on Monday when Aadhya refused?
qa.a: He may have been frustrated or a bit worried, but he let it go, which shows he chose patience over a fight.

grounding: Shows a toddler refusing the potty to claim control over her own body, and a father offering choices and pausing instead of pressing.

passage: Chetan, two, sat on the doorstep staring at his uncle's phone, mouth open, perfectly still. "Chetan, milk!" called his mother Leela from inside. No answer. She came out, gently took the phone, and Chetan screamed, arms out. Leela sat down beside him on the step. "Look, Chetan, the neighbour's calf!" She pointed across the lane. He hiccuped, wiped his nose, and slowly turned to look, still sniffling.

qa.q: What did Leela point out across the lane?
qa.a: She pointed out the neighbour's calf.

qa.q: What was Chetan probably feeling when the phone was taken away?
qa.a: He was distressed and wanted the bright screen back, as his scream and reaching arms show. The lights had held his attention so tightly he did not answer his mother.

qa.q: What could Leela do to limit the phone while still helping Chetan?
qa.a: Keep phone time short and share it with him, and offer hands-on play, outdoor time and things to look at.

qa.q: What might it be like for Leela when Chetan does not answer her calls?
qa.a: She may feel worried or shut out, and a little frustrated, since her son is so wrapped up in the screen that he does not hear her.

grounding: Shows a toddler frozen in front of a phone who screams when it is taken, and a mother redirecting him to something real.

passage:
Monday. Papa, Uday, switched off the cartoon. Two-year-old Pallavi threw herself on the floor and kicked. Uday knelt. "I know, you're sad. The cartoon is finished." He held her until she sniffled.
Wednesday. Same cry, shorter. Uday stayed calm and kept the screen off.
Saturday. "After this one, cartoon is done, then blocks," said Uday. Pallavi whimpered, then crawled over to the blocks and started stacking.

qa.q: What did Uday offer Pallavi after the cartoon on Saturday?
qa.a: He said, "After this one, cartoon is done, then blocks."

qa.q: What is Pallavi feeling when she throws herself on the floor?
qa.a: She is feeling sadness and frustration that the cartoon ended, not bad manners, which is why a hug helps.

qa.q: How did Uday hold the limit without a fight?
qa.a: He stayed calm, kept the screen off, named her sadness, gave a hug, and offered a new activity, so the cries got shorter.

qa.q: How might Uday have felt on Monday while Pallavi kicked on the floor?
qa.a: He may have felt tempted to give in or a little embarrassed, but he steadied himself and kept the limit gently.

grounding: Shows a toddler throwing herself down when the screen goes off, and a father who stays calm, holds the limit, hugs and offers a new activity.

passage: At dinner time in their city flat, Akash sat over his laptop with a deadline. To keep Aparna quiet, he handed her the phone with a cartoon. She watched, still and silent. Then she looked up and pointed at the window. "Papa, look, look!" A pigeon sat on the ledge. Akash, eyes on the screen, said "Mm-hm." She said it again. This time he shut the laptop, lifted her up to the glass and said, "Bird! A grey bird." She squealed and tapped the window.

qa.q: What was on the window ledge that Aparna pointed at?
qa.a: A pigeon was sitting on the window ledge.

qa.q: What was Aparna wanting when she said "Papa, look, look!"?
qa.a: She was probably excited by the pigeon and wanted her father to share the moment, since the cartoon gave her something to watch but not a person.

qa.q: What could Akash do about the phone and his daily time with Aparna?
qa.a: Use the phone as a tool now and then, not a babysitter, and make time each day to talk and play with her.

qa.q: How might Akash have felt when he first said "Mm-hm" and later when he shut the laptop?
qa.a: He was probably stressed by the deadline at first, and perhaps a little guilty and glad when he noticed how much the pigeon mattered to her.

grounding: Shows a toddler handed a phone to keep quiet who gets stimulation but no person until her father looks up and joins her.

passage:
A dog barked behind the fence. "Wuff! Wuff!" Dilnaz froze, then ran to Maria with her arms up. "Mama, up! Up!"
"I've got you. That's a loud dog," said Maria, lifting her. "He's behind the fence. We can stand here."
Dilnaz hid her face, then peeked. "Doggy... far."
"Yes, far away. Shall we wave?"
"Bye, doggy," whispered Dilnaz, clutching Maria's collar.

qa.q: Where was the dog when it barked?
qa.a: The dog was behind the fence.

qa.q: What was Dilnaz feeling when she froze and later peeked, and what does it show?
qa.a: She was frightened at first, and her peeking and saying "Doggy... far" show curiosity slowly returning.

qa.q: What should Maria do the next time Dilnaz meets a dog?
qa.a: Keep a safe distance, comfort her, and let her curiosity come back slowly without pushing her to touch.

qa.q: What would change if Maria had pushed Dilnaz to pat the dog?
qa.a: Dilnaz would probably have been more frightened and learned that her fear does not count, so her trust in Maria might weaken. 🤍

grounding: Shows a toddler terrified by a barking dog running to her mother, who comforts her and keeps a safe distance while curiosity returns.

passage:
Monday. The neighbour's cow stood by the fence. Ujjwal, two, pointed and laughed. "Moo! Moo!" Dada held him up to see.
Tuesday. Ujjwal wanted to feed her some grass. Dada showed him an open, flat hand. "Gentle, gentle," he said, holding Ujjwal's wrist. The cow licked the grass off.
Wednesday. Ujjwal squirmed to run to the cow. Dada caught his hand. "Together. Slowly." He stayed right beside him.

qa.q: What sound did Ujjwal make when he saw the cow?
qa.a: He said, "Moo! Moo!" and laughed.

qa.q: What was Ujjwal feeling about the cow, and what shows it?
qa.a: He felt delight and affection, since he laughed, pointed and wanted to touch and feed her.

qa.q: Why does Dada stay right beside Ujjwal even when the cow is calm?
qa.a: A toddler cannot judge when an animal might be unsafe, so Dada shows gentle hands and keeps close. 😊

qa.q: How might Dada feel watching Ujjwal with the cow?
qa.a: Dada is probably happy to see his grandson's joy, but also watchful, because he knows Ujjwal cannot tell when the cow could be unsafe.

grounding: Shows a toddler laughing at a cow, saying its sound and wanting to feed it, while his grandfather models gentle hands and stays close.
